children: shares traded nearly 4% higher at around $64.22 on Friday after the company successfully launched another Electron rocket, marking its 16th mission of 2026.
lifted off from the Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand and successfully deployed an Earth observation satellite into a 500-kilometer circular low Earth orbit for a confidential customer.
The launch brings the company's total Electron missions to 95, underscoring the company’s growing launch cadence.
Its next Electron mission is expected before the end of September for another commercial constellation operator.

For investors, the steady pace of launches remains a key part of Rocket Lab’s growth story. With global launch capacity under pressure, reliable and frequent access to space can give satellite operators greater certainty around deployment schedules.
However, on the YTD performance side, the stock has underperformed the broader S&P 500 (
) market with -8.57% returns, as compared with the index's 10.90% returns over the same period.
